title: They saw His glory…
paragraphs:
They saw His glory…
but still didn’t get it.

And if we’re honest—
sometimes, neither do we.

Three men stood on a mountain with Jesus.
Not in a sermon.
Not in a story.

His face blazed like the sun. (Matthew 17:2)
His clothes flashed white like lightning.

Then—Moses. Elijah.
History itself standing beside Him.

This wasn’t just a moment.
This was revelation.

He saw glory—
and still tried to manage it.
Have you ever tried to “organize” what God was trying to transform?

Have you ever felt something holy…
and reduced it into something comfortable?

Because Peter wasn’t rebelling.
He was misplacing.

He put Jesus in the same category
as everything else sacred.
“This is My Son… whom I love… with Him I am well pleased. Listen to Him.” (Matthew 17:5)

Not your system.
Not your preference.
But here’s the part most people miss—

When the voice stopped…
when the fear settled…
“And they saw no one except Jesus.” (Matthew 17:8)

God will sometimes strip away even good things
to reveal the only thing that saves.
We don’t struggle because we hate God.
We struggle because we try to add to Him.

Jesus + tradition
Jesus + control
Jesus + hidden pride
Jesus + delayed obedience
But salvation has never been “Jesus plus.”
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not by works…” (Ephesians 2:8–9)

We build identities around moments instead of surrender.
We protect experiences instead of obeying His voice.
We chase encounters but resist repentance.

You don’t need another spiritual high.
You need a surrendered heart.

Some of you felt God before.
You cried.
You promised.
You said, “This time I’ll change.”

A little compromise.
A little delay.
A little pride that whispers,
“I’ll follow… later.”
This is where grace walks in.

Because the same Jesus shining on that mountain
is the same Jesus who walked down…
“For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us…” (2 Corinthians 5:21)

Your sin—paid.
Your shame—carried.
Your soul—redeemed.

You don’t just admire Jesus.
You follow Him.

Some people love the idea of Jesus…
but refuse the authority of Jesus.

You are not called to be a collector of spiritual moments.
You are called to be a follower of the Son.

You are not defined by what you felt on the mountain…
but by who you obey in the valley.

He didn’t leave them in fear.
He called them forward.
And He’s doing the same right now.

What are you still trying to hold on to
that God is asking you to release?

What “extra” have you added
that’s keeping you from only Jesus?

Not to build another tent.
Not to chase another feeling.

Turn from sin.
Lay down pride.
Come back to the voice.

And if you’re hungry for deeper truth,
not to impress you, but to anchor you
so your faith survives beyond the moment.

We’re going deeper into the moment after the mountain…
because that’s where most faith quietly breaks.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
